summary: Build a traditional, elegant 23rd anniversary website for the user's parents with all site content in Hindi and less emphasis on "family come together" messaging, but remove/omit the background audio/music feature and remove/omit photo-related parts (photo gallery/intake) from the site.
architectural_notes: Website should feel traditional and elegant (not Gen Z / overly lovey-dovey), suitable for an arranged-marriage context.
All website content should be in Hindi (including navigation labels and section copy).
Avoid/limit "family come together" / reunion-focused messaging; keep tone traditional and couple-centered.
Set the anniversary/marriage date to 6 Feb 2003 in the site's editable config/constants.
Parents' names to use across the site: Mother = Shivani Tiwari; Father = Ravindra Tiwari (set in centralized config/constants).
Wherever the site displays parents’ names, use the labels “PAPA” and “MUMMY” (per user preference) instead of formal names, unless the user later requests otherwise.
Remove/omit the background soundtrack/audio player feature.
Remove/omit photo-related parts (gallery/intake/photo display) from the site.
Remove/omit the “Humari Kahani” section/content and avoid overly lovey-dovey phrasing; keep tone respectful and suitable for an arranged-marriage context.
Preserve the previously approved/old Hindi site text and only remove/exclude the specific sections/phrases the user requested to omit; avoid accidentally deleting other copy.
known_issues: User reports that site text is missing/removed; needs restoration of the old text except for explicitly excluded parts.

existing_features.title: Create a complete, responsive, single-page anniversary website for the parents’ 23rd anniversary with clear navigation (top navbar or in-page anchor links) and the following sections: Hero/Welcome, About/Note, Timeline (year-by-year or milestone-based), Photo Gallery, Family Messages, and a Closing/Blessing section.

Apply a cohesive, traditional-elegant visual theme (colors, typography, spacing, dividers) suitable for an arranged-marriage context: warm neutrals (e.g., ivory, maroon, gold accents) and classic typography; avoid a Gen Z/stylish “lovey-dovey” aesthetic. Use Tailwind consistently across all sections.

Add a background music feature for an old Indian song: include an audio player UI with Play/Pause and Volume controls, and implement respectful autoplay behavior (do not force autoplay; allow the user to start playback; optionally remember user choice during the session). The audio file must be loaded as a frontend static asset.

Implement a Timeline section with a structured dataset (e.g., an array of milestones) that can be easily edited in code, and render it as a clean vertical timeline (or card list) with year/title/description fields.
Implement a Photo Gallery section that supports multiple images (as static assets), renders them in a responsive grid, and allows viewing a larger version in a modal/lightbox when clicked.

Implement a Family Messages section that displays a list of messages (name + short message) from family members, using a structured dataset that can be edited in code. Include optional support for a scanned handwritten letter image as part of this section (as a static asset).

Add a “23 years in numbers” highlights block (e.g., 23 years, months, approximate days) rendered as simple stat cards. Ensure all numbers are computed in code from a single source value (23 years) so they can be updated easily.
Add an optional “Video Montage” embed area that supports a local video asset or an external video URL (configured in code) and renders it in a responsive container without breaking layout.

Create a small set of editable content/config constants (parents’ names, date/year, short welcome note, blessings/quote) in one place and wire the entire site to use them, so the user can customize without hunting through many files.
Add generated decorative static images (subtle traditional motif background and section dividers) and render them in the UI (as static assets in frontend/public/assets/generated).

Translate/localize all user-facing website copy to Hindi, including section headings, navbar labels, button/CTA text, helper text, footer text, and any dialog/lightbox labels derived from config or hardcoded in components.

Revise the site’s Hindi content to remove or significantly reduce “family came together / families united” emphasis and instead keep the tone traditional, respectful, and focused on the couple’s journey and anniversary blessing.

Add a clear “photo intake” workflow so the user can add many photos easily: update the gallery configuration and/or gallery implementation to support a larger set of photos, and add explicit in-project instructions (in code comments near the gallery config) describing exactly where to put images, what filenames/formats are supported, and how to add/extend captions/alt text.

Fix/verify the background audio (“voice”) feature so that music playback works end-to-end: ensure the referenced audio asset path is valid, the audio loads successfully, the player is visible, and user interaction reliably starts playback. Add a user-visible Hindi hint in the player UI for cases where browser autoplay restrictions require tapping Play.

Update the centralized anniversary configuration to set the parents’ wedding date to 6 February 2003 (replacing the current placeholder date) and ensure the updated date is reflected wherever the site displays the wedding date.

Diagnose and fix why images are not rendering by ensuring all image URLs used in the Hero photo, Photo Gallery grid, Lightbox, and Handwritten Letter resolve correctly in the deployed environment (including any non-root base path). Update the code so image URLs are built using the app base URL (e.g., via a small utility that prefixes `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`) instead of assuming absolute `/assets/...` always works.

Add robust runtime handling for missing/broken images across the site: when an `` fails to load, show a styled fallback UI (keeping the site’s existing Hindi localization) and log a helpful console warning that includes the failing `src`. Apply this to Gallery thumbnails, Lightbox image, Hero framed photo, and handwritten letter preview.

Update the centralized anniversary configuration so the parents’ names are set to Father: Ravindra Tiwari and Mother: Shivani Tiwari, and ensure the updated names appear everywhere the site renders `anniversaryContent.parentsNames` (e.g., the Hero section heading).

Update the centralized anniversary configuration so the displayed parents’ names are exactly “PAPA” and “MUMMY” (replacing the current values), and ensure every UI location that renders `anniversaryContent.parentsNames` reflects this change (e.g., the Hero heading).

Ensure the specified website text remains in Hindi and is not translated or replaced with English anywhere it appears in the UI (including headings, labels, helper text, buttons, and dialog/lightbox copy). If any recent change introduced English copy, revert it back to the prior Hindi phrasing.
Remove the background music feature from the website UI so no audio player is rendered and no audio playback logic is included in the app runtime.
Remove all photo-related parts from the website, including the Photo Gallery section and any photo lightbox interactions.
Remove photo usage from the Hero section so the hero no longer displays a framed photo or any gallery-sourced image.
Remove the handwritten letter image feature from the Family Messages section so the section contains only text-based messages and no letter image preview or letter lightbox.
Update the centralized anniversary configuration to remove photo/audio configuration fields and related inline instructions that are no longer applicable after removing photo/audio features.
Remove the “Humari Kahani” (About/Story) section from the single-page site so it is no longer rendered, linked in the navbar, or tracked in the scroll-spy active section logic.

Revise the site’s written content to remove/avoid “lovey-dovey” romantic phrasing and keep the tone respectful, traditional, and appropriate for an arranged marriage (without making the text negative). Update any affected centralized copy so it remains consistent across the UI.

Restore the website’s previous (“old”) Hindi copy across all rendered sections (Hero, Highlights, Timeline, Messages, Closing Blessing, Navbar, Footer), keeping the content as it was before the recent change, except for the specific parts that the user previously requested to exclude (e.g., removed photo-related features, removed music player, and removed “Humari Kahani” section).

Update the centralized content source so that all restored copy comes from the single content/config module (instead of being scattered or hardcoded), and ensure every section reads from that centralized content to prevent future accidental text loss.

Add a lightweight regression check in the UI to make missing-copy issues obvious during review: if any required text fields from the centralized content/config are empty/undefined, show a visible fallback message in Hindi and log a console warning indicating which field is missing.

Edit the Timeline content so it matches the user’s requested single milestone: Year "2003" with date "06" (digits) and the event text in Hindi (e.g., "शादी/विवाह"). Remove the other existing timeline milestones so only this one remains. Ensure all non-digit text in the timeline milestone is Hindi.

Add a new dedicated section for comments from different people (text-only), with all user-facing copy in Hindi (digits may remain as digits). The comments data must be editable from the centralized content module, and the section must be reachable from the navbar and included in scroll-spy active section tracking.

Update the centralized timeline dataset in `frontend/src/anniversary/content.ts` to match the user-provided milestones (2003–2020) and add a few additional positive placeholder milestones that are clearly marked as editable.

Add a visitor comment submission feature in the Comments section: provide a form (name + comment) that lets site visitors submit a comment, persist submitted comments in the Motoko backend, and display submitted comments in the Comments section UI.

Update the Comments section UI so the submitted comments list is displayed as a comment section directly under the comment submission box (form), rather than appearing as a separate, visually distant block.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create the complete 23rd anniversary website (traditional/elegant style) including sections like homepage, timeline, gallery, family messages, and background old Indian song soundtrack.
Translate/localize the entire anniversary website content into Hindi (all section headings, body text, labels, and UI copy).
Revise/remove overly "family come together" themed copy; keep messaging traditional, respectful, and focused on the couple/anniversary tone.
Update the website’s centralized content/config to set the parents’ names to Shivani Tiwari (mother) and Ravindra Tiwari (father) and reflect them wherever names are displayed.
Update the site copy/config where parents’ names are shown to display “PAPA” and “MUMMY” instead of the current names/text.
Remove/omit the background audio/music player feature and remove/omit all photo-related parts (photo gallery/intake/display) from the website.
Remove the “Humari Kahani” section/part from the site and further reduce any overly “lovey-dovey” content; keep tone nice, respectful, and appropriate for an arranged-marriage context.
Edit the Timeline section content to reflect the specified milestone: “2003 06 Feb” (digits as-is) with the event text in Hindi (e.g., marriage/शादी).
Add a new section for comments/messages from different people (text-based, in Hindi; digits allowed where needed).
Update the Timeline section to include the user-provided multiple milestones (2003–2020) and add a few additional positive milestones, all rendered in the existing Hindi site style.
Add a visitor comments feature: a new section with a form that lets site visitors leave a comment (name + message) and displays submitted comments.
In the visitor comments section, display submitted comments as a comment list/section directly under the comment submission box (form).

projectName: Build a complete traditional 23rd anniversary website (parents) with music, timeline, gallery, and messages
